description:
The ADR-004 machinery beyond the per-endpoint discipline (which every epic carries as a quality gate): TTL tier registry per endpoint class, in-memory hot-event structures (availability counters, event snapshots) with write-path invalidation, hot-event designation (manual + automatic), cache kill-switch for incidents, staleness tests, and an on-sale read load test proving database reads stay flat while buyer traffic scales.

**Conditions of Success:**
- On-sale load test at the festival-scale NFR (~50-100k capacity, 100k+ queued buyers): buyer-facing read RPS scales while database read load stays near-flat for hot events
- A stale 'sold out'/'available' display decays within its declared tier TTL; correctness always restored at claim time (ADR-002)
- Kill-switch bypasses caches per service without redeploy; staleness/invalidation covered by automated tests
- Storefront call budget audited: one aggregated call per page view, client refresh cadence driven by response TTLs

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map) · docs/adr/ADR-004-cache-first-read-path.md

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1). Note: the per-endpoint TTL discipline itself is NOT deferred to this epic — it is a quality gate on every read-endpoint story from US-002 onward (ADR-004).
Backlog grilling 2026-07-12 (owner decisions): load-test COS quantified at festival scale.

### Implementation readiness - CONCERNS

Decomposed 2026-08-04 into five vertical slices, TKT-204..TKT-208. Each is end-to-end for what it claims and demoable on its own; none is a horizontal layer.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | OK | `make check` on every child; browser evidence on TKT-208 only, which is the only child that can change rendered output |
| Vertical slices, one reviewable PR each | OK | C1 is a prefactor (mechanical), C2/C3 one service each, C4 the harness, C5 the storefront |
| Prefactoring split out first | OK | TKT-204 is the prefactor: the tier registry exists so C2/C3's cache lifetime and the response header cannot disagree |
| Ordered by dependency, no forward dependency | OK | 204 -> 205 -> {206, 207}; 208 independent |
| AC verifiable everywhere | OK | Every COS is a counter, a state, or a written artifact. No "works correctly" |
| Links + cycle check | OK | Three `blocked-by` edges, a tree, no cycle |
| Context-memo baked per child | OK | All five, `capturedAt` 2026-08-04, `governingAdrs` re-resolved against `docs/adr/` today rather than copied from the epic |
| No unvalidated assumption a child silently depends on | CONCERN | See concerns 1 and 3 |

**Mapping to the epic's four COS** - every one is owned, none is orphaned:

| Epic COS | Owner |
|---|---|
| On-sale load test: read RPS scales, database read load flat | TKT-207 (proves what TKT-205/206 ship) |
| Stale sold-out/available decays within its tier; correctness restored at claim time | TKT-205, TKT-206 |
| Kill-switch bypasses caches per service without redeploy; staleness/invalidation tested | TKT-205 (builds it), TKT-206 (extends it) |
| Storefront call budget audited; refresh cadence driven by response TTLs | TKT-208 |

**Concerns:**

1. **Hot-event *designation* is carved out of the epic, deliberately** (affects TKT-205). The epic's description names "hot-event designation (manual + automatic)"; **no epic COS requires it**, and population-by-access delivers the same operational result without an operator surface to build, document and get wrong. Recorded as a decision on TKT-205 rather than silently dropped. If TKT-207's load proof shows access-driven population insufficient, that is a follow-up ticket with evidence behind it.

2. **Two caching layers will stack on catalog's event reads** (affects TKT-206). The storefront's SSR `PageDataCache` already fronts exactly those three reads (ADR-004 amendment TKT-128). A second layer with an independent TTL adds its staleness to the first unless invalidation is authoritative end-to-end. TKT-206's plan is required to state the total worst-case staleness, not just catalog's own.

3. **TKT-208 carries one open `uncertainties` item with `owner: human`** - whether the festival page's HTML should become cacheable is a product staleness judgement, not a technical one. Under this run's owner-waived gates the agent decides it and writes the reason into ADR-004. Flagged so the decision is visible in the thread rather than absorbed into an implementation.

4. **TKT-207 touches the gate's smoke suite**, which already has a live flake (TKT-149: a single 5xx in 250 requests fails `TestOnsaleLoadProof`). A read stage that is more flake-prone than the write stage would tax every future ticket. Called out as a review focus, not a blocker.

**Verdict: CONCERNS** - proceedable. The structure holds and every epic COS has an owner; the four concerns are named risks the owner can take eyes-open, and three of the four are already written into the affected child's own readiness comment.

---

**Gate 1 waived by the repo owner** for this run (process experiment, fully autonomous Ready-to-Done). The epic and all five children were moved `Backlog -> Ready` by the agent on the owner's standing instruction rather than by a human drag. Recorded here so the board history shows this epic was never human-prioritized child by child.
